newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh ruling party leads in by-election.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh ruling party leads in by-election.

text.p: A candidate of Bangladesh's ruling Awami League on Tuesday took the lead in a parliamentary by-election boycotted by the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), election commission officials said.
They said the polls in northern Thakurgaon were peaceful, but turnout was low with only about 40 percent of voters casting ballots.
The seat fell vacant with the death of a ruling party member.

The officials said in five out of 111 centres the Awami League's Ramesh Chandra Sen polled 4,147 votes against 2,520 by his nearest rival, Z.H.N. Islam of the Jatiya Party headed by former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad.

The BNP of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia and the fundamentalist Jamaat-e-Islami vowed not to participate in any polls as long as the Chief Election Commissioner, Mohammad Abu Hena, held office.
Both parties accused Hena of favouring the Awami League in last year's general elections, although international observers said the polls were free and fair.
